title: Model-Route Fusion Canvas — comparative dashboard with token-category waterfall
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Design a compact, side-by-side comparison canvas that surfaces per-model and per-route performance signals (latency P95/P99, throughput, token breakdowns, cache hit ratio) and a novel token-category waterfall that reconciles latency and cost impact by token type (prompt, completion, system, cached). Scope: 1) a main fusion canvas that lets users compare up to 3 model+route combinations, 2) a token-category waterfall visualization that aggregates token counts and estimated cost contribution, 3) quick interaction modes: pin/lock, inline diff, and time-window brushing, 4) exportable CSV/PNG and links to trace and request logs. Acceptance criteria: UI mocks in Figma, annotated chart-specs for implementation, accessibility color tokens, PM/Eng sign-off, and a wrapped handoff including a CSS token guide and component list.
design_notes: Tile-based main canvas: each tile is a model+route card with sparkline for throughput and latency band, large numeric KPIs, and a micro-waterfall preview.
Comparison mode overlays: allow inline diff shading of two tiles to show token and latency deltas (green improvement, orange regression).

Token-category waterfall: stacked waterfall ordering should be prompt -> system -> completion -> cached (positive/negative delta for cache hits), with per-token-cost multiplier applied in tooltip for estimated $ contribution.
Latency attribution: show estimated latency contributed by model compute vs. network vs. decoding (heuristic using kv-cache hits and token sizes) so teams can decide batching/quantization levers.
Scale decisions: default time window is 1h; user can switch to 1m/5m/24h. For long windows use sampling and heatmap overlay for burst detection.
Trade-offs: waterfall uses aggregated per-minute buckets to keep performance; precise per-request waterfall available via a 'microtrace' link.
Accessibility: ensure three-way color palette with patterned fills for token categories to be readable for colorblind users.
Differentiator: integrate cost impact (estimated $/1k tokens) next to throughput so PMs can immediately tie perf changes to unit economics.
Componentization: design tokens, KPI number component, sparkline with percentile band, waterfall micro-chart, and tile header with model/version selector.
Decision: use quantized color scale for latency deltas and non-linear scale for throughput to avoid over-emphasizing spikes.
chart_specs: Main KPIs: numeric tiles for P50/P95/P99 latency (ms), throughput (req/s), average tokens/request; source: per-route aggregation; update frequency: 10s.
Sparkline: stacked area for throughput with latency percentile band overlay; x-axis: time, y-left: req/s, y-right: latency ms (opacity band for P50-P99).

Token-category waterfall: x-axis: time or single aggregation bucket; bars: stacked segments for prompt, system, completion, cached; cached displays as negative delta when present; tooltip shows token counts, percent of total, and estimated cost in USD using cost table mapped to model family.
Comparison overlay: when two tiles are selected, delta waterfall shows increases in red and decreases in green; include a toggle to normalize by requests or by tokens.
Microtrace jump: every tile has a link to request-level traces; microtrace opens a swimlane that lines up tokens with kernel selection events where available.
Aggregation rules: default rollup = sum for tokens and throughput; latency uses histogram-derived percentiles computed on the server side and rendered client-side for banding.
review_feedback: PM Sara Lopez: Love the cost-first watermarking; ask to add a filter for customer tier (hosted/dedicated/private) because cost math differs across deployments.
Eng lead Jonas Meyer: Ensure chart specs include sampling strategy for 24h and 7d windows; need explicit API endpoints (range + granularity) for efficient queries.
Backend owner Priya Nair: Flag - cache delta estimation requires additional KV metrics; created ENG ticket requests below.
Design review notes (03/10): Adjusted color ramp to match global tokens; added patterned fills for cached segments for accessibility.
QA note: Verify CSV export schema includes: timestamp, model, route, requests, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cached_tokens, est_cost_usd.
